questions.question:
Identify the INCORRECT sentence(s).

a. Some organisms use simple food material obtained from inorganic sources in the form of carbon dioxide and water.

b. Other organisms utilise complex substances which are broken down into simpler ones before they can be used for the upkeep and growth of the body.

c. Heterotrophic organisms include plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The statement "Heterotrophic organisms include plants" is incorrect. Plants are generally autotrophic organisms, meaning they produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• Heterotrophic organisms are those that cannot synthesize their own food and rely on other organisms for nutrition.
 
• Examples of heterotrophic organisms include animals, fungi, and many bacteria.
 
• Autotrophic organisms, such as plants, algae, and some bacteria, use light or chemical energy to synthesize food from inorganic substances.
 
• The other statements (a and b) correctly describe the nutritional modes of organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autotrophic Nutrition**

 
 
• Involves the use of simple inorganic substances to produce food.
 
• Photosynthesis is a common example, where plants convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen using sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Heterotrophic Nutrition**
 
 
• Involves consuming complex organic substances for nutrition.
 
• Includes various modes such as holozoic, saprophytic, and parasitic nutrition.
 
 
 
• **Mixotrophic Nutrition**
 
 
• Some organisms exhibit both autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition.
 
• Examples include certain protists and some plants like Venus flytrap.

questions.question: Milk is a mixture of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**water, fat, protein, etc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Milk is a complex mixture containing water, proteins, fats, lactose, minerals, and vitamins.
 
• The main protein in milk is casein, which constitutes about 80% of the protein content in cow's milk.
 
• Milk fat is present in the form of emulsified globules and is a significant source of energy.
 
• Lactose, also known as milk sugar, is the primary carbohydrate found in milk.
 
• Minerals like calcium and phosphorus are abundant in milk, making it essential for bone health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein Types in Milk**

 
 
• Casein and whey are the two primary types of proteins found in milk.
 
• Whey protein is a by-product of cheese production and is often used in protein supplements.
 
 
 
• **Milk Processing**
 
 
• Milk undergoes various processing steps like pasteurization to ensure it is safe for consumption.
 
• Homogenization is another process that breaks down fat molecules so that they remain integrated rather than separating as cream.
 
 
 
• **Milk Varieties**
 
 
• There are different types of milk available such as whole milk, skim milk, and lactose-free milk.
 
• Each type caters to specific dietary needs and preferences.

questions.question: Which tissue is responsible for movement in our body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muscular tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Muscular tissue is responsible for the movement of the body and its parts.
 
• There are three types of muscular tissue: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle.
 
• Skeletal muscles are attached to bones and cause voluntary movements.
 
• Cardiac muscle tissue is found only in the heart and is responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscle tissue is found in walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestines, and blood vessels and is responsible for involuntary movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nervous tissue**

 
 
• Nervous tissue is responsible for transmitting nerve impulses and is found in the brain, spinal cord, and nerves.
 
• It plays a crucial role in controlling and coordinating body activities.
 
 
 
• **Epithelial tissue**
 
 
• Epithelial tissue forms the lining of internal and external surfaces of the body, including skin and the lining of organs.
 
• It provides protection and is involved in absorption, secretion, and sensation.
 
 
 
• **Connective tissue**
 
 
• Connective tissue supports, binds, and protects other tissues and organs.
 
• It includes bone, cartilage, adipose tissue, and blood.

questions.question: Select the correct option for liquid connective tissue.

__
 
• Blood is considered a connective tissue because it has a matrix, called plasma, in which cells are suspended.
 
• It plays a crucial role in transporting nutrients, oxygen, and waste products throughout the body.
 
• Blood consists of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, each serving distinct functions.
 
• It helps in maintaining homeostasis by regulating pH, temperature, and water content of cells.
 
• Blood also plays a vital role in the immune system, helping to protect the body against diseases and infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cartilage**

 
 
• It is a flexible connective tissue found in joints, rib cage, ear, nose, bronchial tubes, and intervertebral discs.
 
• Cartilage provides support and cushioning to the body structures and is more rigid than muscle but more flexible than bone.
 
 
 
• **Adipose connective tissue**
 
 
• This tissue stores fat and provides insulation and cushioning for the body.
 
• It plays a role in energy storage and helps to protect organs.
 
 
 
• **Areolar connective tissue**
 
 
• This is a loose connective tissue that holds organs in place and attaches epithelial tissue to underlying tissues.
 
• It contains a variety of cell types and fibers that provide support and elasticity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of epithelial tissue?

options.text: Covers most organs and cavities within the body
Seperated from the underlying tissue by a cellular, non fibrous basement membrane

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Epithelial tissues have no intercellular spaces, making them tightly packed and forming continuous sheets.
 
• They cover most organs and cavities within the body, providing a protective barrier.
 
• Epithelial tissues are separated from the underlying tissue by a basement membrane, which is non-cellular and fibrous.
 
• The basement membrane is composed of proteins like collagen and glycoproteins, providing support and anchoring the epithelium.
 
• Epithelial tissues play roles in protection, secretion, absorption, and sensation in various organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Connective Tissue**

 
 
• Connective tissues support, bind, and protect other tissues and organs.
 
• They have various types, including loose connective tissue, dense connective tissue, cartilage, bone, and blood.
 
 
 
• **Muscle Tissue**
 
 
• Muscle tissues are responsible for movement in the body.
 
• They are categorized into three types: skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle tissues.
 
 
 
• **Nervous Tissue**
 
 
• Nervous tissues are specialized for the conduction of electrical impulses.
 
• They consist of neurons and glial cells, with functions in sensing stimuli and transmitting signals.

questions.question: Which of the following environmental factors plays a role in sex determination of few reptiles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temperature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Temperature-dependent sex determination (TSD) is a phenomenon where the environmental temperature during a critical period of embryonic development determines the sex of the offspring.
 
• This type of sex determination is observed in some reptiles, including certain species of turtles, crocodiles, and lizards.
 
• The specific temperature range and the critical period for sex determination can vary among different species.
 
• In many cases, higher temperatures tend to produce one sex (often females), while lower temperatures produce the other sex (often males).
 
• TSD is an important adaptive mechanism that helps maintain a balanced sex ratio in natural populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genetic Sex Determination (GSD)**

 
 
• In GSD, sex is determined by specific chromosomes (e.g., XX/XY system in mammals).
 
• This type of sex determination is common in birds, mammals, etc.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Factors Other Than Temperature**
 
 
• Other environmental factors such as the availability of resources, population density, and social interactions can also influence sex ratios in some species.
 
• These factors can impact the development and survival of offspring, indirectly affecting sex determination.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Implications**
 
 
• Understanding TSD is crucial for the conservation of endangered reptile species, as changes in environmental temperatures due to climate change can skew sex ratios.
 
• Conservation efforts may involve managing nesting sites to ensure balanced sex ratios for population stability.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms does NOT show asexual reproduction by means of fission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthworm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually and not by asexual means like fission.
 
• Plasmodium, Amoeba, and Leishmania are known to reproduce asexually through fission.
 
• Amoeba reproduces by binary fission, where the organism splits into two equal halves.
 
• Plasmodium reproduces through multiple fission, where one cell divides into many smaller cells.
 
• Leishmania also reproduces through binary fission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• It is a type of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes.
 
• Offspring are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, and spore formation.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction common in prokaryotes and some single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• The parent organism divides into two approximately equal parts.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**
 
 
• In multiple fission, the nucleus divides several times before the cell divides into multiple new cells.
 
• This is commonly observed in some protozoa like Plasmodium.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by budding?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hydra is a genus of small, fresh-water organisms that belong to the phylum Cnidaria.
 
• Reproduction in Hydra occurs through a process called budding, where a new individual develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• The bud initially remains attached to the parent organism and then detaches to become an independent organism.
 
• Budding is an asexual mode of reproduction, allowing for rapid population growth under favorable conditions.
 
• Hydra can also reproduce sexually, but budding is the most common and frequent mode of reproduction in these organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earthworm**

 
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually through a process called copulation, where two worms exchange sperm.
 
• They are hermaphrodites, meaning each individual possesses both male and female reproductive organs.
 
 
 
• **Frog**
 
 
• Frogs reproduce sexually with external fertilization, where the female lays eggs and the male fertilizes them outside her body.
 
• Frogs undergo a complex life cycle including egg, tadpole, and adult stages.
 
 
 
• **Cockroach**
 
 
• Cockroaches reproduce sexually with internal fertilization, where the male deposits sperm inside the female's body.
 
• They lay eggs in protective cases called oothecae, which hatch into nymphs that undergo several molts before becoming adults.

questions.question: Which of the following animals shows the power of regeneration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Planaria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Planaria** are well-known for their remarkable regenerative capabilities.
 
• They can regenerate any part of their body, making them a subject of extensive biological research.
 
• This regeneration is possible due to the presence of a large number of stem cells called **neoblasts**.
 
• Planaria can regenerate not only their body parts but also their nervous system, including the brain.
 
• Their regenerative ability is an example of **asexual reproduction**, specifically through a process called **fission**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earthworm**

 
 
• Earthworms also have regenerative abilities but to a lesser extent than planaria.
 
• They can regenerate lost segments, but the extent of regeneration is limited and varies among species.
 
 
 
• **Tick**
 
 
• Ticks do not have significant regenerative abilities.
 
• They primarily rely on their hardy exoskeleton and parasitic lifestyle for survival.
 
 
 
• **Leech**
 
 
• Leeches have some regenerative capabilities, particularly in their nervous system.
 
• However, their regenerative abilities are not as advanced as those of planaria.

questions.question: The ability of a fully differentiated organism to give rise to new individuals from their body parts is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**regeneration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is the ability of a fully differentiated organism to give rise to new individuals from their body parts.
 
• This process is common in certain species such as starfish, planarians, and some amphibians.
 
• In regeneration, cells undergo dedifferentiation to form a mass of cells, which then proliferate and differentiate to form new tissues and organs.
 
• Regeneration can occur at the level of tissues, organs, or even entire organisms depending on the species and the extent of damage.
 
• This biological process is crucial for healing and recovery from injuries in organisms capable of regeneration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragmentation**

 
 
• It is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism is split into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new, complete organism.
 
• This method is common in algae, fungi, and some invertebrates.
 
 
 
• **Fission**
 
 
• It is a type of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two or more separate organisms.
 
• Bacteria and protists commonly reproduce through binary fission.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• In budding, a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• Hydra and yeast are examples of organisms that reproduce through budding.

questions.question: Select the process responsible for stability of populations of species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reproduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Reproduction** is the biological process by which new individual organisms are produced from their parents.
 
• It is essential for the **continuation and stability of species**, ensuring that populations can be maintained over generations.
 
• There are two main types of reproduction: **asexual and sexual**. Asexual reproduction involves a single organism or cell, while sexual reproduction involves the combination of genetic material from two parents.
 
• Reproduction allows for the **transfer of genetic information** from one generation to the next, which is vital for the survival of a species.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **natural selection and evolution**, as it introduces genetic variation within a population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mutation**

 
 
• Mutations are changes in the DNA sequence that can lead to genetic variation within a population.
 
• They can be beneficial, neutral, or harmful and play a role in the process of evolution.
 
 
 
• **Evolution**
 
 
• Evolution is the process by which different kinds of living organisms develop and diversify from earlier forms over generations.
 
• It involves mechanisms such as natural selection, mutation, gene flow, and genetic drift.
 
 
 
• **Variation**
 
 
• Variation refers to the differences in the genetic makeup and characteristics within and among populations of organisms.
 
• It is essential for the process of natural selection and the overall adaptability of a species.

questions.question: In the food vacuole of which organism, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones which then diffuse into the cytoplasm?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amoeba is a single-celled organism that uses a food vacuole for digestion.
 
• The food vacuole in Amoeba engulfs food particles through a process called phagocytosis.
 
• Inside the food vacuole, complex substances are broken down into simpler ones by digestive enzymes.
 
• The simpler substances then diffuse into the cytoplasm to be used by the cell.
 
• This process ensures that Amoeba can efficiently obtain nutrients from its environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium**

 
 
• Plasmodium is a parasitic protozoan, known for causing malaria in humans.
 
• It has a complex life cycle involving both humans and mosquito hosts.
 
 
 
• **Spirogyra**
 
 
• Spirogyra is a filamentous green alga, known for its spiral chloroplasts.
 
• It reproduces both sexually and asexually through fragmentation and conjugation.
 
 
 
• **Lichen**
 
 
• Lichen is a symbiotic association between a fungus and a photosynthetic partner, usually algae or cyanobacteria.
 
• They are known for their ability to colonize harsh environments, including bare rocks.

questions.question: Identify the single cell organism.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amoeba**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a single-celled organism commonly found in freshwater environments.
 
• It belongs to the **protist kingdom** and is known for its ability to change shape due to its flexible cell membrane.
 
• Amoebas move by extending their **pseudopodia** (false feet), which are temporary projections of the cell.
 
• They feed through a process called **phagocytosis**, where they engulf food particles with their pseudopodia.
 
• Amoebas reproduce asexually through a process called **binary fission**, where the cell divides into two identical daughter cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seaweed**

 
 
• Seaweeds are multicellular marine algae and are not single-celled organisms.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems, providing food and habitat for marine life.
 
 
 
• **Leech**
 
 
• Leeches are multicellular parasitic or predatory worms belonging to the phylum Annelida.
 
• They are known for their bloodsucking behavior and are used in medical treatments for bloodletting.
 
 
 
• **Liver fluke**
 
 
• Liver flukes are parasitic flatworms belonging to the class Trematoda.
 
• They infect the liver and bile ducts of various mammals, including humans.

The correct answer is __**Earthworm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leishmania reproduces asexually by binary fission, where the organism divides into two equal parts.
 
• Amoeba also undergoes binary fission, a type of asexual reproduction where the cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
• Earthworms reproduce sexually and do not undergo asexual reproduction by means of fission.
 
• Plasmodium, the parasite responsible for malaria, reproduces asexually by multiple fission within the host's red blood cells and liver cells.

• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• A common method of asexual reproduction in prokaryotes and some single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Involves the division of a single organism into two parts, each of which grows into a new organism.
 
 
 
• **Multiple Fission**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where the nucleus divides multiple times before the cell splits into many new cells.
 
• Commonly seen in some protozoa and algae, like Plasmodium.
 
 
 
• **Hermaphroditism**
 
 
• A condition in which an organism has both male and female reproductive organs.
 
• Common in some invertebrates like earthworms, as well as in many plants.

questions.question: Malarial parasite shows which type of asexual reproduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multiple fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Malarial parasite, Plasmodium, reproduces asexually through a process known as **multiple fission**.
 
• During multiple fission, the nucleus of the parasite divides multiple times before the cell splits into several daughter cells.
 
• This process allows for rapid multiplication of the parasite within the host's body.
 
• Multiple fission typically occurs in the liver cells and red blood cells of the infected host.
 
• It is a crucial part of the parasite's life cycle, contributing to the spread and severity of malaria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes like bacteria.
 
• Involves the division of a single organism into two equal parts, each with a copy of the DNA.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**
 
 
• A process where organisms regrow lost or damaged parts.
 
• Commonly seen in species like starfish and planarians.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• A type of asexual reproduction seen in organisms like yeast and Hydra.
 
• Involves the formation of a new organism from a small projection growing on the parent organism.

questions.question: In organisms such as Amoeba, the splitting of the two cells during division can take place in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**any plane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In organisms such as Amoeba, cell division occurs through a process called binary fission.
 
• During binary fission, the nucleus of the Amoeba divides first, followed by the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• The splitting of the two cells during division in Amoeba can take place in any plane.
 
• This flexibility in the plane of division allows Amoeba to reproduce efficiently under varying environmental conditions.
 
• Amoebas are unicellular organisms, meaning they consist of a single cell that carries out all vital biological processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission in Bacteria**

 
 
• Bacteria also reproduce through binary fission, where the DNA replicates and the cell splits into two identical daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Mitotic Cell Division**
 
 
• In multicellular organisms, mitotic cell division ensures that each new cell receives an identical copy of the parent cell's DNA.
 
• This type of division is essential for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction in eukaryotes.
 
 
 
• **Meiotic Cell Division**
 
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four genetically diverse daughter cells.
 
• This process is crucial for sexual reproduction, contributing to genetic variation in offspring.

questions.question: Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the scientific name of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A species of yeast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** is a species of yeast and is widely used in **biotechnology, baking, and brewing industries.**
 
• It is commonly referred to as **brewer's yeast** or **baker's yeast** due to its role in fermenting sugars to produce alcohol and in baking bread by creating carbon dioxide gas.
 
• This yeast is a model organism in molecular and cellular biology because it is a **eukaryotic microbe**, which shares similar cellular processes with higher organisms.
 
• It is used extensively in research to study **cell division, genetics, and metabolic pathways.**
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** reproduces both sexually and asexually, making it highly adaptable to different environments.
 
• It is one of the first organisms to have its **entire genome sequenced.**
 
• This species of yeast is integral to the production of **bioethanol**, which is a renewable energy source.
 
• It is also utilized in the production of various **pharmaceuticals and vaccines.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A species of amoeba**__

 __
 
• Amoebas are single-celled organisms that belong to the kingdom **Protista**.
 
• They are characterized by their **ability to change shape** due to the movement of pseudopodia (false feet).
 
• Amoebas are found in **freshwater, saltwater, soil, and as parasites** in animals.
 
• Unlike yeasts, amoebas do not have a cell wall and are not used in industrial or research applications like **Saccharomyces cerevisiae.**
 
 
 
• **A type of virus**__
 __
 
• Viruses are **non-cellular infectious agents** that require a host cell for replication.
 
• They consist of genetic material (either **DNA or RNA**) enclosed in a protein coat.
 
• Unlike yeast, viruses are not living organisms and cannot be used for fermentation or other biochemical processes.
 
• Viruses are studied primarily for their role in **disease causation and vaccine development.**
 
 
 
• **A type of bacteria**__
 
 
• Bacteria are single-celled organisms that belong to the **prokaryotic domain.**
 
• Unlike yeast, bacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.
 
• Some bacteria are used in food production (e.g., **Lactobacillus** for yogurt) but have different biochemical pathways compared to yeast.
 
• Bacteria are widely used in **genetic engineering, bioremediation, and antibiotic production.**

questions.question: When milk gets converted into curd, the bacteria improves its nutritional quality by increasing _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**vitamin B12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When milk is converted into curd, **Lactic acid bacteria** (commonly Lactobacillus) play a crucial role in the fermentation process.
 
• These bacteria improve the nutritional quality of curd by increasing its **vitamin B12 content**.
 
• Vitamin B12 is essential for maintaining healthy nerve cells and producing DNA and red blood cells.
 
• The fermentation process enhances the bioavailability of certain nutrients, making curd nutritionally superior to milk.
 
• Curd is also beneficial for gut health due to the presence of probiotics, which aid in digestion and improve immunity.

questions.question: What are the number of chromosomes in a human male germ cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23 Chromosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Human male germ cells, also known as sperm cells, contain **23 chromosomes**.
 
• These chromosomes are **haploid**, meaning they contain a single set of chromosomes.
 
• During fertilization, the 23 chromosomes from the sperm combine with 23 chromosomes from the female germ cell (egg) to form a diploid zygote with **46 chromosomes**.
 
• The 23 chromosomes include **22 autosomes** and 1 sex chromosome, which can be either X or Y.
 
• Human males are characterized by the presence of one X and one Y chromosome, denoted as **46,XY** in diploid cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chromosomes**:

 
 
• Structures within cells that contain DNA and carry genetic information.
 
• Humans typically have 23 pairs of chromosomes in each somatic cell, totaling 46 chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Diploid and Haploid**:
 
 
• Diploid cells (2n) have two sets of chromosomes, one from each parent.
 
• Haploid cells (n), like sperm and egg cells, have only one set of chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization**:
 
 
• The process where a sperm cell and an egg cell combine to form a zygote.
 
• Ensures that the offspring inherits genetic material from both parents.
 
 
 
• **Sex Chromosomes**:
 
 
• Determine the biological sex of an individual.
 
• In humans, females have two X chromosomes (XX) and males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY).

questions.question: Leishmania reproduces by:

__
 
• Leishmania is a genus of trypanosome protozoa and is responsible for the disease known as leishmaniasis.
 
• Leishmania reproduces through a process called binary fission.
 
• In binary fission, the organism divides into two equal halves, each becoming a new organism.
 
• For Leishmania, this binary fission occurs in a definite plane, ensuring proper division and distribution of cellular components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leishmaniasis:**

 
 
• A disease caused by protozoan parasites of the genus Leishmania.
 
• It is transmitted to humans by the bites of infected female phlebotomine sandflies.
 
• Leishmaniasis has several forms, including cutaneous, mucocutaneous, and visceral leishmaniasis.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission:**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where a single organism divides into two parts, each of which can grow into a new organism.
 
• Common among prokaryotes such as bacteria, and some protozoa.
 
• Ensures rapid population growth under favorable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Protozoa:**

__

• **Mycelium**

 
 
• The mycelium is the vegetative part of a fungus, consisting of a network of hyphae.
 
• It is the main mode of vegetative growth and plays a critical role in nutrient absorption.
 
 
 
• **Sporangia**
 
 
• Sporangia are structures produced at the tips of hyphae where asexual spores are formed.

• **Spores**

• **Rhizoids**

questions.question: Seeds that are dispersed by animals often:

options.text: are very small and light weight

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**have hooks or edible flesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Seeds dispersed by animals often have hooks or barbs that attach to the fur or feathers of animals, allowing them to be carried to new locations.
 
• Some seeds have fleshy, edible parts that attract animals. When animals consume these fruits, the seeds are later excreted, often at a distance from the parent plant.
 
• This method of dispersal helps in the spreading of plants over large areas, enhancing their survival and propagation chances.
 
• Examples include seeds of burdock that cling to animal fur and berries that are eaten by birds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoochory:** The dispersal of seeds by animals is known as zoochory. It is a form of mutualism where both the plant and the dispersing animal benefit.
 
• **Endozoochory:** This occurs when seeds are dispersed through the digestive tract of animals. Seeds that pass through the digestive system may have higher germination rates due to the removal of the fleshy part and exposure to digestive enzymes.
 
• **Epizoochory:** This is the dispersal of seeds by attachment to the outside of animals. Seeds have specialized structures like hooks, barbs, or sticky surfaces to cling to animal fur or feathers.
 
• **Mutual Benefits:** Plants benefit from enhanced seed dispersal, while animals gain nutritional value from the fruits they consume.
 
• **Examples:** Common examples of zoochory include berries eaten by birds, acorns collected by squirrels, and seeds of burdock that attach to the fur of mammals.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary reason why all multi-cellular organisms do not reproduce by fragmentation?

options.text: They have a random arrangement of cells.
They have specialised cells organised into tissues and organs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They have specialised cells organised into tissues and organs.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Multi-cellular organisms consist of specialised cells that perform specific functions, which are organised into tissues and organs.
 
• Fragmentation is a type of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into fragments, each capable of growing independently into a new organism.
 
• The complexity and organisation of tissues and organs in multi-cellular organisms prevent them from simply fragmenting into new, fully functional organisms.
 
• Specialisation of cells ensures that different functions such as digestion, respiration, and reproduction are efficiently carried out by different tissues and organs.
 
• Examples of multi-cellular organisms include humans, animals, and plants, which rely on this complex organisation for survival and reproduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Specialisation**

 
 
• Refers to the process where generic cells develop into specific cell types with distinct functions.
 
• Examples include muscle cells, nerve cells, and blood cells.
 
 
 
• **Tissues**
 
 
• Groups of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.
 
• Examples include epithelial tissue, connective tissue, muscle tissue, and nervous tissue.
 
 
 
• **Organs**
 
 
• Structures composed of multiple tissues that work together to perform complex functions.
 
• Examples include the heart, lungs, liver, and kidneys.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Reproduction without the involvement of gametes (sex cells).
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, and fragmentation.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation**
 
 
• A form of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into fragments, each of which can develop into a complete organism.
 
• Common in simpler organisms such as starfish and some plants.

questions.question: In the context of plant and animal kingdoms, what does chemotaxonomy primarily focus on?

options.text: The classification of organisms based on their ecological roles.
The classification of organisms based on their chemical composition.

The classification of organisms based on their morphological characteristics.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The classification of organisms based on their chemical composition.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chemotaxonomy is a method of biological classification based on the chemical composition of organisms.
 
• This approach utilizes the presence of specific chemical compounds such as alkaloids, terpenoids, flavonoids, and other secondary metabolites.
 
• It helps in identifying and differentiating species based on their biochemical markers.
 
• Chemotaxonomy is particularly useful in the classification of plants and microorganisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkaloids:** Naturally occurring chemical compounds containing basic nitrogen atoms, often found in plants and having significant pharmacological effects.
 
• **Terpenoids:** A large and diverse class of organic compounds produced by a variety of plants, especially conifers, and by some insects. They often have strong odors and can serve ecological roles.
 
• **Flavonoids:** A group of plant metabolites thought to provide health benefits through cell signaling pathways and antioxidant effects.
 
• **Secondary Metabolites:** Organic compounds that are not directly involved in the normal growth, development, or reproduction of an organism, often playing a role in plant defense.
 
• **Biochemical Markers:** Molecules that can be measured in biological samples, acting as indicators of biological and pathogenic processes or pharmacological responses to a therapeutic intervention.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about aneuploids?

options.text: One or more chromosomes of a chromosome set either missing or having more copies
Unequal distribution of chromosomes to opposite poles
Usually results from irregular meiotic division
Organisms having more than two sets of chromosomes in each cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Organisms having more than two sets of chromosomes in each cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Aneuploidy refers to the presence of an abnormal number of chromosomes in a cell, which can be either more or fewer chromosomes than a typical chromosome set.
 
• This condition often results from errors during cell division, such as nondisjunction, where chromosomes do not separate properly during meiosis or mitosis.
 
• Common examples of aneuploid conditions include Down syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner syndrome (monosomy X), and Klinefelter syndrome (XXY).
 
• The statement "Organisms having more than two sets of chromosomes in each cell" describes polyploidy, not aneuploidy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aneuploidy:** A condition in which the number of chromosomes is not an exact multiple of the haploid number for the species, leading to an imbalance.
 
• **Polyploidy:** A condition where an organism has more than two complete sets of chromosomes, common in plants but rare in animals.
 
• **Nondisjunction:** The failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during cell division, leading to aneuploidy.
 
• **Trisomy:** A type of aneuploidy characterized by the presence of an extra chromosome, resulting in three copies of a chromosome instead of two.
 
• **Monosomy:** A type of aneuploidy where there is a missing chromosome, resulting in one copy of a chromosome instead of the usual two.

questions.question:

__
 
• **Gonorrhoea** is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by the bacterium *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*.
 
• **Syphilis** is another sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium *Treponema pallidum*.
 
• Both infections are primarily transmitted through sexual contact, including vaginal, anal, and oral sex.
 
• Early detection and treatment with antibiotics are crucial to prevent long-term complications and transmission to sexual partners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AIDS** (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome) is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) and is not a bacterial infection but a viral infection.
 
• **Neisseria gonorrhoeae** can infect the genital tract, mouth, and rectum, leading to symptoms such as painful urination and discharge.
 
• **Treponema pallidum** causes syphilis, which progresses in stages: primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary, each presenting different symptoms.
 
• Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can be prevented through the use of condoms, regular screening, and maintaining a mutually monogamous relationship with an uninfected partner.

questions.question: Amphibians have a _______ chambered heart.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Amphibians, such as frogs and salamanders, have a three-chambered heart.
 
• The heart consists of two atria and one ventricle.
 
• The three-chambered heart allows for some separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• This structure is an evolutionary adaptation suited to their dual life in water and on land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxygenation Process:**

 
 
• In amphibians, the heart pumps both oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which partially mixes in the single ventricle.
 
• This mixed blood is then sent to the lungs and skin for oxygenation and to the rest of the body.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory System:**
 
 
• Amphibians have a double circulatory system, with separate pulmonary and systemic circuits.
 
• This system is more efficient than a single circulatory system but less efficient than a four-chambered heart.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Vertebrates:**
 
 
• Fish have a two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle).
 
• Birds and mammals have a four-chambered heart (two atria and two ventricles), which allows for complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• The three-chambered heart of amphibians represents an intermediate stage in the evolution of the more complex hearts of higher vertebrates.
 
• This adaptation is essential for amphibians' survival in both aquatic and terrestrial environments.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are NOT a parasitic organism?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **Amoeba** is a type of **single-celled organism** found in various water bodies.
 
• Amoebas belong to the **phylum Amoebozoa**.
 
• They are typically **free-living** and do not rely on a host for survival.
 
• Amoebas move and ingest food through a process called **phagocytosis**, using extensions of their cell membrane known as **pseudopodia**.
 
• Unlike parasitic organisms, amoebas do not exhibit a parasitic relationship where they harm a host organism to derive nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ticks**__

 __
 
• **Ticks** are small arachnids that are ectoparasites, meaning they live on the outside of their host.
 
• They feed on the blood of mammals, birds, and sometimes reptiles and amphibians.
 
• Ticks can transmit various diseases to humans and animals, including Lyme disease.
 
 
 
• **Cuscuta**__
 __
 
• **Cuscuta**, also known as dodder, is a genus of parasitic plants.
 
• These plants have no chlorophyll and rely on host plants for nutrients.
 
• Cuscuta wraps around host plants and forms haustoria to absorb nutrients directly from them.
 
 
 
• **Lice**__
 
 
• **Lice** are small, wingless insects that are parasitic on mammals and birds.
 
• They live in the hair or feathers of their hosts and feed on blood or skin.
 
• Lice infestations can cause itching and discomfort and are often spread through close contact.

questions.question: Modes of reproduction in various organisms depend on the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**body design of the organisms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mode of reproduction in organisms is significantly influenced by their **body structure and design**.
 
• Organisms with simpler body designs, such as single-celled organisms, typically reproduce asexually through processes like binary fission or budding.
 
• More complex organisms, including most animals and plants, often reproduce sexually, involving specialized reproductive organs and processes.
 
• The body design can determine the feasibility and efficiency of different reproductive strategies, ensuring the survival and adaptation of species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**

 
 
• Involves a single parent and produces offspring identical to the parent.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, fragmentation, and spore formation.
 
• Examples include bacteria (binary fission) and yeast (budding).
 
 
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Involves the combination of genetic material from two parents to produce genetically diverse offspring.
 
• Involves specialized reproductive cells called gametes (sperm and egg).
 
• Common in animals, plants, and many other organisms.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Strategies**
 
 
• Reproductive strategies can be influenced by environmental factors, availability of mates, and evolutionary pressures.
 
• Some organisms can switch between asexual and sexual reproduction based on environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation and Survival**
 
 
• Reproductive modes are crucial for the adaptation and survival of species in changing environments.
 
• Genetic diversity from sexual reproduction can enhance the resilience of populations to diseases and environmental changes.

• This location is crucial because **sperm formation** requires a temperature that is **lower than the normal body temperature**.
 
• The normal body temperature is about **37 degrees Celsius**, while the scrotal temperature is around **34 degrees Celsius**, which is ideal for **spermatogenesis**.
 
• A lower temperature is necessary to maintain the **viability and motility of sperm**.
 
• The scrotum acts as a natural **thermoregulator**, ensuring that the testes remain at a temperature conducive to sperm production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Normal body temperature**__
 
 
• Sperm formation does not occur optimally at the normal body temperature; it requires a slightly cooler environment.

questions.question: In which of the following life processes is the creation of a DNA copy, a basic event?

__
 
• The creation of a **DNA copy** is a fundamental event in the process of **reproduction**.
 
• During reproduction, organisms produce new individuals, and this process involves the **replication of DNA** to ensure that the offspring receive the correct genetic information.
 
• The **DNA** replication process ensures that each new cell or organism has the same genetic information as its parent.
 
• This process is critical for the **continuity of genetic information** from one generation to the next.
 
• Both **sexual and asexual reproduction** involve the creation of a DNA copy, ensuring genetic material is passed on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Respiration**__

 __
 
• Respiration is the process through which organisms convert **oxygen and glucose** into **energy**, carbon dioxide, and water.
 
• This process does not involve the creation of **DNA copies**.
 
 
 
• **Excretion**__
 __
 
• Excretion is the process of removing **waste products** and toxins from the body.
 
• This process involves the **kidneys, liver, and skin** but does not involve the replication of **DNA**.
 
 
 
• **Circulation**__
 
 
• The **circulatory system** is responsible for transporting **blood, nutrients, gases, and wastes** to and from the cells of the body.
 
• It does not include the process of creating **DNA copies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hydra** is a genus of small, freshwater organisms known for their remarkable regenerative abilities.
 
• In Hydra, **budding** is a form of asexual reproduction where new individuals develop from the body wall of the parent organism.
 
• The budding process involves **regenerative cells** that proliferate and differentiate to form a new organism.
 
• Once the bud matures, it detaches from the parent Hydra and becomes an independent organism.
 
• This method of reproduction allows Hydra to rapidly increase their population under favorable environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regeneration:**

 
 
• Regeneration is the process by which some organisms replace or restore lost or amputated body parts.
 
• Hydra is one of the simplest organisms with extensive regenerative abilities.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction:**
 
 
• Asexual reproduction is a mode of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes.
 
• Offspring produced through asexual reproduction are genetically identical to the parent organism.
 
 
 
• **Stem Cells:**
 
 
• In Hydra, regenerative cells are akin to stem cells in more complex organisms.
 
• These cells can differentiate into various cell types necessary for forming new tissues and organs.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Factors:**
 
 
• The rate of budding in Hydra can be influenced by environmental factors such as water temperature, food availability, and water quality.
 
• Optimal conditions can lead to an increased rate of budding and population growth.

questions.question: Animals like hydra and planaria can be cut into any number of pieces and each piece grows into a complete organism. This is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**regeneration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is the process by which certain organisms replace or restore lost or damaged tissues, organs, or limbs.
 
• Animals like hydra and planaria exhibit remarkable regenerative abilities, allowing them to grow into a complete organism from a small piece of their body.
 
• In planaria, stem cells called neoblasts play a crucial role in regeneration.
 
• Hydra can regenerate due to the presence of interstitial cells that can differentiate into various cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budding**

 
 
• Budding is a form of asexual reproduction commonly seen in yeast and hydra.
 
• In this process, a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud due to cell division at one particular site.
 
• The bud remains attached to the parent organism while it grows and develops, and detaches when it is mature.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation**
 
 
• Fragmentation is another form of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into fragments, each of which develops into a new organism.
 
• This method is observed in organisms like starfish, sponges, and certain annelids.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**
 
 
• Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction common among prokaryotes like bacteria.
 
• In this process, the organism duplicates its genetic material and then divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.

__
 
• **Condoms** act as a **mechanical barrier** by physically preventing the sperm from reaching the egg, thereby avoiding fertilization.
 
• They are made of materials such as **latex, polyurethane, or lambskin**, which provide an effective barrier to sperm and sexually transmitted infections (**STIs**).
 
• Condoms are one of the most widely used contraceptive methods and are effective in preventing **unintended pregnancies** and reducing the risk of **HIV/AIDS** and other STIs.
 
• They are easy to use, widely available, and do not require a prescription, making them a popular choice worldwide.
 
• Both **male and female condoms** are available, but male condoms are more commonly used.
 
• Condoms do not involve hormones, which makes them suitable for individuals who cannot or do not want to use hormonal contraceptives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __

• Contraceptive pills are an example of **hormonal contraception**, not a physical device.
 
 
 
• **Copper T — Hormonal imbalance**__
 __
 
• This is incorrect because **Copper T** is a type of **intrauterine device (IUD)** that works by releasing **copper ions**, which are toxic to sperm. It does not cause hormonal imbalance.
 
• Copper IUDs are non-hormonal and function as a long-term reversible contraceptive method.
 
 
 
• **Tubectomy — Chemical barrier**__
 
 
• This is incorrect because **tubectomy** is a form of **permanent surgical sterilization** in females. It involves blocking or cutting the fallopian tubes to prevent the egg from reaching the uterus.
 
• It is not a chemical barrier but a surgical procedure.

__
 
• The **urethra** in males serves as a common passage for both **urine** and **sperm.**
 
• It is a tube-like structure that connects the **urinary bladder** to the external part of the body for the excretion of **urine.**
 
• During ejaculation, sperm from the **testes** passes through the urethra and exits the body.
 
• The **urethra** is part of both the **urinary system** and the **reproductive system** in males.
 
• This dual function is facilitated by a special muscular valve called the **internal urethral sphincter**, which prevents urine from mixing with sperm during ejaculation.
 
• Located at the tip of the penis, the urethra opens to the outside of the body, allowing for the discharge of fluids.
 
• It plays a crucial role in maintaining proper functioning of the male reproductive and urinary systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• The **vas deferens** is a tube that transports sperm from the **testes** to the **urethra.**
 
• It is part of the male reproductive system but does not serve as a passage for urine.
 
• The vas deferens plays a role in storing and carrying sperm during ejaculation.

 __
 
• The **scrotum** is a pouch-like structure that houses the **testes.**
 
• It maintains the optimal temperature for sperm production but does not function as a passage for urine or sperm.

• It is part of the urinary system and does not play any role in the passage of sperm.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of connective tissue, EXCEPT:

__
 
• **Tracheid:**
 
• Tracheids are elongated, tubular cells found in the xylem of vascular plants.
 
• They are primarily responsible for the transport of water and minerals throughout the plant.
 
• Tracheids have thick, lignified cell walls that provide structural support to the plant.
 
• They are a component of vascular tissue, which is a plant tissue, not connective tissue.
 
• Tracheids are dead at maturity, leaving only their cell walls to function in transport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bone:**
 
• Bone is a specialized connective tissue that forms the skeletal framework in vertebrates.
 
• It consists of a hard, mineralized matrix containing calcium phosphate and collagen fibers.
 
• Bone provides structural support, protects internal organs, and serves as a site for mineral storage.
 
• It also contains bone marrow, which is involved in blood cell production.
 
• Bone is a living tissue that is constantly being remodeled.
 
• **Blood:**
 
• Blood is a fluid connective tissue that circulates throughout the body.
 
• It consists of plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.
 
• Blood transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in immune response and blood clotting.
 
• Blood is vital for maintaining homeostasis.
 
• **Cartilage:**
 
• Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue that provides support and cushioning to joints and other structures.
 
• It consists of chondrocytes embedded in a matrix of collagen and elastic fibers.
 
• Cartilage lacks blood vessels, which results in slow healing.
 
• It is found in various locations, including the ears, nose, and joints.
 
• Cartilage provides a smooth surface for joint movement.

questions.question: Many nerve fibres are bound together by which tissue and make up a nerve?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Connective tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Connective tissue is one of the four main types of tissue in the body, the others being epithelial, muscle, and nervous tissues.
 
• Nerve fibers are bound together by connective tissue, which provides structural support and protection.
 
• In nerves, connective tissue layers are classified into endoneurium, perineurium, and epineurium.
 
• The endoneurium surrounds individual nerve fibers, the perineurium surrounds bundles of nerve fibers (fascicles), and the epineurium surrounds the entire nerve.
 
• This hierarchical organization of connective tissue ensures that nerves are protected and can function effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Connective Tissue:**

 
 
• Loose connective tissue: Includes areolar, adipose, and reticular tissues.
 
• Dense connective tissue: Includes dense regular, dense irregular, and elastic tissues.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Connective Tissue:**
 
 
• Provides structural support to organs and tissues.
 
• Protects and insulates internal organs.
 
• Stores energy reserves, particularly in the form of fat.
 
• Transports substances within the body, particularly through blood, which is a type of connective tissue.
 
 
 
• **Nerve Structure:**
 
 
• Nerves are composed of neurons, the fundamental units of the nervous system that transmit signals.
 
• Neurons are surrounded by myelin sheaths, which are produced by Schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Connective Tissue Disorders:**
 
 
• Examples include Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Marfan syndrome, and systemic lupus erythematosus.
 
• These disorders can affect the integrity and function of connective tissues, leading to a variety of symptoms and complications.

• **Stratified squamous epithelium** is a type of epithelial tissue that consists of multiple layers of flat cells.
 
• The primary function of this tissue is to provide **protection** against mechanical stress, dehydration, and microbial invasion.
 
• The outermost layer of the skin, known as the **epidermis**, is composed of stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• These cells in the skin are **keratinized**, meaning they contain keratin, a protein that helps in waterproofing and providing strength.
 
• Stratified squamous epithelium is also found in other parts of the body, such as the **oesophagus and oral cavity**, but the skin's epidermis is the most prominent example.

• **Epithelial Tissue**

 
 
• Epithelial tissues are one of the four basic types of tissues in the body, along with connective tissue, muscle tissue, and nervous tissue.
 
• They cover the body surfaces, line body cavities, and form glands.
 
• Epithelial tissues are classified based on the number of layers (simple or stratified) and the shape of the cells (squamous, cuboidal, or columnar).
 
 
 
• **Keratin**
 
 
• Keratin is a type of protein found in the skin, hair, and nails.
 
• It provides structural strength and helps protect cells from damage or stress.
 
 
 
• **Oesophagus**
 
 
• The oesophagus is a muscular tube that connects the throat (pharynx) with the stomach.
 
• It is lined with non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which provides protection from abrasion due to food passage.
 
 
 
• **Skin Layers**
 
 
• The skin is composed of three main layers: the epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis.
 
• The epidermis is the outermost layer, primarily made up of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
 
• The dermis lies beneath the epidermis and contains connective tissue, blood vessels, and nerve endings.
 
• The hypodermis, also known as the subcutaneous layer, contains fat and connective tissue that insulates and cushions the body.

• Composed of cube-shaped cells.
 
• Commonly found in glandular tissues and in the lining of the kidney tubules.
 
• Involved in absorption, secretion, and excretion processes.
 
 
 
• **Ciliated Columnar Epithelium:**
 
 
• Contains column-like cells with cilia on the surface.
 
• Lines the respiratory tract and the fallopian tubes, helping in the movement of mucus or eggs.

• Specialized for secretion and forms the glands.
 
• Can be unicellular (goblet cells) or multicellular (salivary glands).
